# anchor

> Beta durable-execution framework for existing Go code: wrap functions with Activity/Step/Event, run a worker (a pull loop that can be the submitting process itself), and code becomes durable. On crash or retry the workflow re-executes from the top; recorded calls return instantly from the ledger and the first unrecorded call executes for real. Three concepts only: ledgers (durable truth, in tables the caller already owns; adapters validate and never migrate), queues (flow and clock, disposable and rebuildable from the ledger), and workers (no inbound surface). Record identity is name#occurrence, with nested calls scoped under their parent's key, so code rolls forward across releases with no version, patch, or pinning APIs. Outside a run every wrapped function is a plain Go call.

Go module `github.com/urmzd/anchor` (a library, zero third-party dependencies at the root). Adapters are separate modules: `adapters/postgres` (pgledger on existing tables, pgqueue on FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED, with an optional delta-table DeltaLog woken by LISTEN/NOTIFY, and pgkit, the stack's shared Postgres plumbing: advisory-locked migrations and a LISTEN/NOTIFY Listener) and `adapters/redis` (redisqueue: ZSET lease queue plus a Redis Streams delta log).

## Key Concepts

- Ledger: runs plus write-once memoized records; `Accept`, `Complete` (first terminal write wins), `Load`, `Record` (first write wins on (runID, key), losers adopt), `ListPending(ctx, before time.Time, cursor run.PendingCursor, limit int)` (the janitor seam, cursor-paginated); optional `ledger.RunGetter{GetRun}` capability: a point read that `Handle.Result` polling prefers over `Load`; optional `ledger.PrefixReader{RecordsWithPrefix(ctx, runID, prefixes...)}`: a run's records by literal key prefix
- Queue: run IDs under fenced, time-bounded claims; `claim -> heartbeat* -> settle | release | expire`; `Claim` returns `Item{RunID, Attempt, Failures}`: Attempt is the fencing token and increments on every claim, Failures is the retry budget and moves only on genuine failure (`Release(ctx, it, delay, failed bool)` with failed=true, or an expiry reclaim); Settle-and-re-enqueue never touches Failures, so waiting is free; `MaxAttempts` bounds Failures, never claims
- Worker: claim, replay to the frontier, exactly one outcome per claim, persisted on a cancellation-detached context (graceful shutdown releases with failed=false, burning no budget); janitor paginates the ENTIRE pending set from ledger truth
- Replay: memo hit verifies kind, input hash, and recorded codec content type (mismatch = terminal); record keys are parent-scoped ("process-order#0/charge-payment#0"); a non-retryable failure surfaces as `*run.RecordedError` on every attempt including the first (branch on it or its message, not errors.Is of your original error); events with no record park the run (`ErrParked`); retryable failures write nothing and burn one failure
- Wait as absence: `Event` parks at zero budget cost; call it from the workflow body, not inside a nested activity (`Client.Signal` targets top-level event keys); resume = write the event record + enqueue (`Client.Signal` sugar, your own table insert, or the janitor backstop)
- Deltas: `Emit` streams advisory flow into the queue-side `DeltaLog` capability, split by attempt/seal dividers; never truth, never re-streamed after checkpoint

- docs/architecture/overview.md: the three concepts, package DAG, module layout, the two adapters, capability pattern, roadmap
- docs/design/replay.md: replay algorithm, claim protocol, the 12-row failure-mode table, park/resume, delta consumer algorithm, versioning rules
- AGENTS.md: AI-facing conventions, commands, rules, extension guide
- CONTRIBUTING.md: development workflow and commit convention
- examples/quickstart: the README hero, runnable (kills its own worker mid-run)
- examples/chaos: cross-process SIGKILL recovery test against real Postgres and Redis

## API Cheatsheet

- Wrap: `anchor.Activity(name, fn) *ActivityFn[I, O]`; `a.Call(ctx, in)`; `a.CallKeyed(ctx, key, in)` (order-independent keys); `anchor.Step(ctx, name, fn)` (inline non-determinism); `anchor.Event[O](ctx, name)` (wait as absence); `anchor.Emit(ctx, payload)`; `anchor.PriorDeltas(ctx)`
- Submit: `anchor.New(ledger, queue, opts...) *Client`; `anchor.Start(ctx, c, a, in, opts...) (*Handle[O], error)` (on Accept-success/Enqueue-failure it returns the handle ALONGSIDE the error: the run is durable and the janitor recovers it); `anchor.Exec` (Start + Result); `anchor.HandleFor[O](c, runID)`; `h.Result(ctx)`; options `WithRunID` (the submit idempotency key), `WithMaxAttempts` (bounds FAILED executions; waiting is free), `WithParent`
- Observe and resume: `c.Signal(ctx, runID, name, payload)`; `c.Watch(ctx, runID, cursor)` (needs the DeltaLog capability)
- In-run context: `anchor.FromContext(ctx) (RunInfo, bool)`; `anchor.InRun(ctx)`; `anchor.IdempotencyKey(ctx)` = "runID:recordKey"; `anchor.NonRetryable(err)`; `anchor.Void`
- Consume: `worker.New(ledger, queue, opts...) *Worker` (pkg/worker); `w.Run(ctx)`; options `WithLeaseTTL`, `WithHeartbeatEvery`, `WithBackoff`, `WithConcurrency`, `WithJanitorEvery`, `WithCodec`, `WithRegistry`, `WithLogger`
- Postgres: `pgledger.New(pool, mapping) (*Ledger, error)`; `pgledger.Mapping{Runs: RunsMap{Table, RunID, Status, Envelope, CreatedAt, Scope, Defaults}, Records: RecordsMap{Table, RunID, Key, Envelope, Scope, Defaults}}`; `pgledger.DefaultMapping()`; `lgr.Validate(ctx)`; `pgledger.RecommendedDDL(mapping)`; `pgqueue.New(pool, mapping, opts...)` with the same validate/DDL pattern; `pgqueue.NewDeltaQueue(pool, mapping, pgqueue.DefaultDeltaMapping(), opts...)` (queue.Queue + queue.DeltaLog on a delta table, `pgqueue.RecommendedDeltaDDL(dm)`) for Postgres-only streaming; identifiers are lower_snake_case only; uniqueness must be a plain unique index or constraint (partial/expression unique indexes are rejected: ON CONFLICT cannot use them)
- pgkit: `pgkit.Apply(ctx, db pgkit.Beginner, name string, steps ...string) error` (idempotent steps, one transaction, advisory lock derived from name; db is a pool, conn or tx); `pgkit.NewListener(pool, pgkit.WithBuffer(n), pgkit.WithBackoff(lo, hi)) (*Listener, error)`; `l.Listen(ctx, channel) (<-chan pgkit.Notification, error)` (closed when ctx ends; `Notification{Channel, Payload, Resync}`, Resync first and after every reconnect or overflow: re-read state); `l.Listening()`; `pgqueue.WithListener(l)` shares it with a DeltaQueue
- Redis: `redisqueue.New(client, namespace, opts...)` (queue.Queue + queue.DeltaLog); namespace must be non-empty with no braces (it becomes the cluster hash tag); `redisqueue.WithPollInterval(d)`
- Sentinels (pkg/run, match with errors.Is): `ErrNotFound`, `ErrSuperseded`, `ErrAlreadyTerminal`, `ErrAlreadyRecorded`, `ErrNonDeterministic`, `ErrParked`, `ErrMaxAttempts`; memoized non-retryable failures match with errors.As against `*run.RecordedError{Name, Key, Message}`
